question: When was Tephra founded and by whom?
expected_answer: 2019, by Ingrid Halvorsen and Rafe Okafor.

question: Where does the name Tephra come from?
expected_answer: Tephra is volcanic ash and rock thrown out in an eruption. It refers to Mount Meager's last major eruption about 2,400 years ago, which left a tephra layer across the region.

question: How much does the Mackenzie airbag pack cost and when did it launch?
expected_answer: $1,199 CAD. Launched February 3, 2025.

question: Who is Tephra's paid media agency and who are the contacts?
expected_answer: Tarn Digital. Marcus Webb (Account Lead) and Sofia Kim (Analyst).

question: What was Tephra's total revenue in 2025 compared with 2024 and the plan?
expected_answer: $4.36M in 2025, up 4% on $4.20M in 2024, and 7% below the $4.70M plan.

question: What was Tephra's full-year MER in 2025?
expected_answer: 6.3 ($4.36M revenue on $691K paid media spend), above the 6.0 target in the 2025 plan.

question: Why did Meta ROAS drop in March 2025?
expected_answer: The February 11, 2025 Basalt theme migration removed a legacy script in theme.liquid that fired the AvyGearView and Engaged60s custom events. The AG-30 and ENG-60 retargeting audiences shrank (AG-30 from about 23,400 to 5,600), so retargeting CPA rose from $65 to $156 and blended CAC rose to $122 (vs $104 in March 2024). Priya found it March 18; Theo fixed it March 20 with a custom pixel in Shopify Customer Events.

question: Was creative fatigue the reason Meta retargeting performance fell in March 2025?
expected_answer: Not mainly. The agency first blamed creative fatigue because frequency hit 4.1, but frequency was high because the audiences were shrinking. The main cause was the removed custom audience script from the February 11 theme migration.

question: Who discovered the retargeting audience problem in March 2025 and how?
expected_answer: Priya Sandhu, on March 18, 2025. She noticed in Meta Ads Manager that AG-30 had fallen to 5,600 people and ENG-60 to 6,900.

question: What are the AG-30 and ENG-60 audiences?
expected_answer: Meta retargeting audiences. AG-30 is people who viewed avalanche safety products (AvyGearView event) in the last 30 days. ENG-60 is people with 60 seconds of active time on any page (Engaged60s event) in the last 30 days.

question: How long were the custom audience events broken in early 2025?
expected_answer: From February 11 to March 20, 2025, about five and a half weeks. Audiences then took about four weeks to rebuild because they use a 30-day window.

question: How did the TikTok test perform and was it continued?
expected_answer: It ran January 6 to March 31, 2025 at $4,500 per month ($13,500 total). Average CPA $241 against the $140 prospecting CPA target, and average ROAS 1.3. Not continued; confirmed at the Q1 QBR on April 10, 2025.

question: Why were new-visitor sessions lower in April 2025?
expected_answer: Partly because the TikTok test ended on March 31, 2025; TikTok had been a meaningful source of new visitors. April new customers were down 2% year over year.

question: Why did revenue drop so much in May 2025?
expected_answer: It was the normal end of spring touring season. May revenue was 50% below April, but up 6% on May 2024, which showed the same pattern. Nothing was broken.

question: Did the GA4 consent mode change in May 2025 cause lost sales?
expected_answer: No. The May 6, 2025 Consent Mode v2 update lowered GA4 session counts (GA4 went from about 92% to about 84% of Shopify sessions), but Shopify orders and revenue were unaffected.

question: Which data source should be used for revenue and orders after May 2025?
expected_answer: Shopify. GA4 sessions should be treated as directional after the May 6, 2025 consent mode change.

question: Why was revenue flat year over year in June and July 2025 even though Performance Max ROAS doubled?
expected_answer: On June 2, 2025, Tarn moved budget from Search into Performance Max without brand exclusions. PMax picked up branded searches that the brand Search campaign used to capture cheaply, so it took credit for existing demand rather than finding new customers. About 58% of PMax conversions were on brand terms. PMax CPA fell from $68 to $29, but blended CAC rose to $65 (vs $46 in June 2024) and new customers fell. Branded search revenue fell from $25,700 (June 2024) to $14,700 (June 2025).

question: When were brand exclusions added to Performance Max?
expected_answer: August 5, 2025, along with restoring the brand Search budget.

question: What was total Google platform revenue in May vs June 2025?
expected_answer: $59.9K in May and $41.4K in June. It fell even though PMax CPA dropped from $68 to $29 and ROAS rose from 3.6 to 7.8.

question: Did the warehouse move cause July 2025 revenue to be flat?
expected_answer: No. Shipping was paused only July 14 to 15, 2025 and the agency saw no meaningful effect. Flat July revenue was mainly the PMax brand cannibalization.

question: Why did Meta ROAS jump to 5.4 in September 2025?
expected_answer: It wasn't real. On September 9, 2025, Meta Conversions API moved to a server-side gateway that sent the checkout token as event_id while the browser pixel sent the order ID. Meta couldn't deduplicate, so most purchases were counted twice. Meta CPA showed $50 (vs $73 in August), but blended CAC barely moved. Restated September: about a $90 CPA and 3.0 ROAS.

question: Who found the Meta double-counting problem and what evidence did they use?
expected_answer: Jordan Leclerc, on October 6, 2025. Meta reported 163 purchases for October 1 to 5, but Shopify had only 86 orders with Meta UTMs (239 total). In September Meta reported 846 purchases while Shopify had 1,053 orders across all channels.

question: What decision was made based on the inflated September Meta numbers, and what did it cost?
expected_answer: Tarn recommended scaling Meta 35% for October and Priya and Ingrid approved it on September 30. October Meta spend was $56,800 instead of the planned $42,000, without the expected return.

question: What is the rule for event_id on Meta Purchase events?
expected_answer: event_id must be the Shopify order ID on both the browser pixel and the Conversions API gateway.

question: Which dates have inflated Meta purchase data?
expected_answer: September 9 to October 8, 2025.

question: Why was October 2025 revenue down 18% year over year?
expected_answer: Low snow. The early-season snowpack was well below normal through October and most of November, so customers delayed buying hardgoods. Skis and splitboards were down 32% and boots, bindings and uphill gear down 31% year over year. New customers fell from 954 to 740. The first major storm cycle didn't arrive until November 24, 2025.

question: Which product category grew in October 2025 and why?
expected_answer: Avalanche safety and packs, up 14% year over year, because fall avalanche course season drives purchases regardless of snow.

question: Was the October 2025 revenue drop caused by the Meta tracking problem?
expected_answer: No. The tracking problem inflated Meta-reported purchases but didn't change Shopify revenue. The real revenue drop was caused by low snow.

question: Why wasn't the Fissile splitboard in the Black Friday 2025 sale?
expected_answer: It sold out on November 12, 2025. The 2025/26 production run was delayed at the factory (Kestrel Board Works, core material problem), so the shipment slipped from October 30 to December 12. Black Friday was rebuilt around Mackenzie and Matier.

question: Why did the Fissile Meta campaign keep running after Fissile sold out?
expected_answer: Dana's stockout alert went to inventory-alerts@tephra.ca, which only included Dana, Jordan and Ingrid. Priya and Tarn Digital weren't on the list, so the campaign ran until November 21, 2025 and spent $8,400 sending people to a sold-out page. Its CPA went from $142 to $1,050.

question: How many Fissile splitboards sold in November 2025 vs November 2024?
expected_answer: 67 in November 2025 (all between November 1 and 12) vs 106 in November 2024.

question: Why didn't Tephra air freight Fissile boards to cover Black Friday?
expected_answer: Air freighting 25 units would have cost about $6,000 extra, and Dana and Rafe decided the margin on 25 boards didn't cover it.

question: How did Black Friday weekend 2025 perform?
expected_answer: Revenue was up 9% on the same weekend in 2024, helped by the November 24 storm, even without Fissile.

question: When was Fissile back in stock?
expected_answer: December 15, 2025. The 180-unit shipment arrived December 12. Campaigns relaunched December 16.

question: Was December 2025 a bad month, since revenue was lower than November?
expected_answer: No. December was 13% below November, which is normal after Black Friday, but up 9% on December 2024.

question: What tracking or measurement problems did Tephra have in 2025?
expected_answer: Four: (1) February 11 to March 20, custom audience script removed in the theme migration; (2) May 6, GA4 Consent Mode v2 lowered GA4 session counts; (3) June 2 to August 5, Performance Max taking credit for branded search; (4) September 9 to October 8, Meta Conversions API double counting.

question: What changes did Tephra make to prevent these problems in 2026?
expected_answer: A monthly tracking health check (Jordan with Theo), inventory alerts wired into ad campaigns so sold-out products pause, a weekly platform vs Shopify comparison, a pre-launch tracking checklist, and marketing and Tarn added to inventory alerts.

question: When is the office closed over the holidays?
expected_answer: December 24, 2025 to January 1, 2026, reopening January 2, 2026.

question: What was Tephra's blended CAC in 2025 and did it hit the target?
expected_answer: $87 (7,930 new customers on $691K spend), within the $95 target. 2024 was $83.

question: Why did blended CAC go up in June and July 2025 when Performance Max CPA went down?
expected_answer: PMax was taking credit for branded searches from people already looking for Tephra, many of them returning customers, so platform CPA fell without adding new customers. Blended CAC was $65 in June and $68 in July, vs $46 and $47 in 2024.

question: What was the warning sign in September 2025 that Meta's results weren't real?
expected_answer: Meta CPA halved (from $73 to $50) and Meta conversion rate nearly doubled, but blended CAC only improved 6% on last year ($118 vs $127) and Shopify orders didn't match Meta's purchase count.

question: Why wasn't the Pylon splitboard used as the Black Friday headline?
expected_answer: Only 41 units were left, too few to carry a headline offer. Pylon stayed at full price and sold out over Black Friday weekend.

question: When does Tephra launch new products?
expected_answer: All new products launch together at the season launch, September 15 (in 2025: Pylon, Owl, Spearhead, Wedge, Portage, Pioneer, Anderson, Birken, Blowdown, women's Matier and Rohr). The exception was Mackenzie, launched February 3, 2025 after certification testing delayed it from September 2024.

question: Why did summer 2025 AOV go up compared with a normal off-season?
expected_answer: The End-of-Season Sale (May 12 to August 31) sold last season's skis, splitboards and boots at 25 to 40% off, so discounted hardgoods were over half of summer revenue and AOV was about $230.

expected_answer: The documents don't say. Tephra didn't run TikTok in 2024; the first test was January to March 2025.
